title: NEURONOPATHY, DISTAL HEREDITARY MOTOR, AUTOSOMAL RECESSIVE 9
alt_titles: NEUROPATHY, DISTAL HEREDITARY MOTOR, AUTOSOMAL RECESSIVE 9

relationships.phenotype: NEURONOPATHY, DISTAL HEREDITARY MOTOR, AUTOSOMAL RECESSIVE 9

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that autosomal recessive distal hereditary motor neuronopathy-9 (HMNR9) is caused by homozygous mutation in the COQ7 gene (601683) on chromosome 16p12.3.

checks.claim: Autosomal recessive distal hereditary motor neuronopathy-9 (HMNR9) is caused by homozygous mutation in the COQ7 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: we have identified the first example of recessive distal hereditary motor neuropathy caused by a homozygous variation in the COQ7 gene
checks.explanation: Paper reports homozygous COQ7 variant causing recessive dHMN; HMNR9 is OMIM nomenclature.

checks.claim: The COQ7 gene is located on chromosome 16p12.3.
checks.evidence_quote: associated with the identification of a homozygous mutation in the COQ7 gene located on chromosome 16
checks.explanation: Paper states chromosome 16; the band 16p12.3 is standard nomenclature.

paragraphs.text: Autosomal recessive distal hereditary motor neuronopathy-9 (HMNR9) is a neurologic disorder. Jacquier et al. (2023) described slowly progressive distal muscle weakness and atrophy, mainly in the lower limbs. These result from a length-dependent loss of motor nerve function, and sensory involvement is absent or minimal. Some patients have upper motor neuron signs. Other COQ7 mutations cause a more severe, multisystem primary coenzyme Q10 deficiency. In contrast, HMNR9 is mostly limited to the peripheral motor system (Jacquier et al., 2023).

checks.claim: Autosomal recessive distal hereditary motor neuronopathy-9 (HMNR9) is a neurologic disorder.
checks.evidence_quote: Distal hereditary motor neuropathy (dHMN) is a motor inherited neuropathy, resulting in a distal weakness starting in the lower limbs, with a slowly progressive course.

checks.claim: Jacquier et al. (2023) described HMNR9 as featuring slowly progressive distal muscle weakness and atrophy.
checks.evidence_quote: Distal hereditary motor neuropathy (dHMN) is a motor inherited neuropathy, resulting in a distal weakness starting in the lower limbs, with a slowly progressive course.
checks.explanation: Slowly progressive distal weakness; patients also had amyotrophy in the lower limbs and hands.

checks.claim: In HMNR9, the distal muscle weakness and atrophy mainly affect the lower limbs.
checks.evidence_quote: There was evidence of a pure motor axonal neuropathy predominantly affecting the distal part of the lower limbs.
checks.explanation: The paper says the lower limbs are predominantly affected.

checks.claim: In HMNR9, the distal weakness and atrophy result from a length-dependent loss of motor nerve function.
checks.evidence_quote: All of the patients presented with length-dependent pure motor axonal neuropathy, leading to progressive walking difficulties and disability, with childhood onset.
checks.explanation: The paper describes a length-dependent motor axonal neuropathy.

checks.claim: In HMNR9, sensory involvement is absent or minimal.
checks.evidence_quote: He had never complained of sensory symptoms.
checks.explanation: Sensory examinations and sensory nerve conduction were normal; one patient reported mild trouble sensing temperature, consistent with 'absent or minimal'.

checks.claim: Some patients with HMNR9 have upper motor neuron signs.
checks.evidence_quote: The clinical phenotype of dHMN with pyramidal features reported here is suggestive of upper motor neuron involvement.
checks.explanation: Patients II-2 and II-3 had pyramidal signs.

checks.claim: Other COQ7 mutations cause a more severe, multisystem primary coenzyme Q10 deficiency.
checks.evidence_quote: Mutations of COQ7 were previously associated with primary CoQ10 deficiencies (MIM 601683, COQ10D8) encompassing a large spectrum of severe phenotypes.
checks.explanation: The paper also mentions multiorgan failure.

checks.claim: HMNR9 is mostly limited to the peripheral motor system.
checks.evidence_quote: the family studied here presented with a less severe phenotype characterized by isolated neurological damage of motor neurons, despite comprehensive systemic explorations.
checks.explanation: The paper describes isolated damage to the motor neurons.

paragraphs.text: Jacquier et al. (2023) noted that other COQ7 mutations cause primary coenzyme Q10 deficiency. That disorder is more severe and multisystemic than HMNR9 and can include neonatal-onset disease, developmental delay and spasticity. Smith et al. (2023) noted that earlier reports had also associated COQ7 with hearing loss. HMNR9 is therefore allelic to COQ7-related primary coenzyme Q10 deficiency (Jacquier et al., 2023).

checks.claim: Jacquier et al. (2023) noted that other COQ7 mutations cause primary coenzyme Q10 deficiency.
checks.evidence_quote: Mutations of COQ7 were previously associated with primary CoQ10 deficiencies (MIM 601683, COQ10D8) encompassing a large spectrum of severe phenotypes.

checks.claim: COQ7-related primary coenzyme Q10 deficiency is more severe and multisystemic than HMNR9.
checks.evidence_quote: Compared to previously reported patients with COQ7 mutations, the family studied here presented with a less severe phenotype characterized by isolated neurological damage of motor neurons
checks.explanation: The paper also describes the earlier cases as multiorgan disorders.

checks.claim: COQ7-related primary coenzyme Q10 deficiency can include neonatal-onset disease.
checks.evidence_quote: The first patient was reported by Freyer et al. in 2015 with a c.422T>A homozygous substitution associated with encephalo-neuro-nephro-cardiopathy at birth.
checks.explanation: The paper describes disease onset at birth.

checks.claim: COQ7-related primary coenzyme Q10 deficiency can include developmental delay.
checks.evidence_quote: Six families of patients with early childhood onsets and developmental delays were identified.

checks.claim: COQ7-related primary coenzyme Q10 deficiency can include spasticity.
checks.evidence_quote: Wang et al. and Hashemi et al. extended the phenotype of COQ7-associated diseases by reporting two patients affected by hereditary spastic paraplegia associated with developmental delay.
checks.explanation: Spastic paraplegia was reported in earlier cases.

checks.claim: Smith et al. (2023) noted that earlier reports had associated COQ7 with hearing loss.
checks.evidence_quote: While COQ7 has been associated with hearing loss in past reports,,, hearing loss did not segregate with COQ7 variants in this report.
checks.explanation: The Discussion says directly that earlier reports linked COQ7 to hearing loss.

checks.claim: HMNR9 is allelic to COQ7-related primary coenzyme Q10 deficiency.
checks.evidence_quote: Here, we extend the spectrum of COQ7-associated disorders by reporting the first familial cases of patients affected by COQ7 mutation and presenting with a pure distal motor neuropathy.
checks.explanation: Both disorders are caused by mutations in COQ7, so they are allelic.

paragraphs.text: Jacquier et al. (2023) identified a homozygous mutation in the COQ7 gene in a family with recessive distal hereditary motor neuropathy. They noted that COQ7 is one of the main enzymes involved in coenzyme Q10 biosynthesis.

checks.claim: Jacquier et al. (2023) identified a homozygous COQ7 mutation in a family with recessive distal hereditary motor neuropathy.
checks.evidence_quote: We report a family of two brothers and a sister affected by distal hereditary motor neuropathy in whom a homozygous variant c.3G>T (p.1Met?) was identified in the COQ7 gene.

checks.claim: COQ7 is one of the main enzymes involved in coenzyme Q10 biosynthesis.
checks.evidence_quote: By catalysing the hydroxylation of 6-DMQ in mitochondria, COQ7 is one of the main enzymes involved in CoQ10 synthesis.

clinical_synopsis.feature: Upper motor neuron signs in some patients
